extracted.intended_audience: applicants, their agents, International Searching Authorities, receiving Offices, designated Offices, and patent office examiners involved in PCT procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing the conduct, contents, timing, transmittal, and supplementary handling of international searches and related reports under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT). Covers ISAs, applicants, the International Bureau, and designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account results of earlier search (Rule 41.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant requests under Rule 4.12 that the International Searching Authority take into account results of an earlier search and has complied with Rule 12 bis.1:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier search was carried out by the same International Searching Authority (or the same Office acting as ISA), the ISA shall, to the extent possible, take those results into account. If the earlier search was carried out by another ISA or another Office, the ISA may take those results into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account earlier search/classification in priority cases (Rule 41.2/43.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the international application claims priority from earlier applications for which an earlier search was carried out by the same ISA/Office, or where the receiving Office has transmitted copies of earlier search/classification results, the ISA shall or may take those results into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies available from the receiving Office or accessible digital libraries may be taken into account if available in a form acceptable to the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishing the international search report (Rule 42.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for establishing the international search report or the declaration under Article 17(2)(a) is three months from receipt of the search copy by the ISA, or nine months from the priority date, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time limit governs ISA performance for producing the ISR or declaration; the later-expiring of the two limits applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: International search report must be dated and show completion and priority filing dates (Rule 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall be dated and indicate the date the international search was actually completed and shall indicate the filing date of any earlier application whose priority is claimed (or the earliest filing date where multiple priorities are claimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ISR contains explicit dates for search completion and priority claims to allow accurate timing and publication references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification in the ISR (Rule 43.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report shall contain the classification of the subject matter at least according to the International Patent Classification (IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISA effects the classification; if another classification system was used for identification of fields searched, it shall be published by the ISA (see Fields Searched).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of international search report and declarations (Rule 43.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every ISR and any declaration under Article 17(2)(a) shall be in the language in which the international application is to be published, subject to specified exceptions allowing other accepted languages or translations to be used where the ISA so wishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a translation was transmitted under Rule 23.1(b) or furnished under Rule 12.4, the ISA may choose the language of that translation or another language it accepts and which is a publication language under Rule 48.3(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification data required in ISR (Rule 43.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall identify the International Searching Authority which established it by name, and indicate the international application number, the name of the applicant, and the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identification elements must appear clearly on the ISR for proper attribution and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations in the ISR (Rule 43.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall contain citations of the documents considered to be relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method for identifying cited documents is governed by the Administrative Instructions. Citations of particular relevance should be specially indicated; citations not relevant to all claims shall be cited in relation to the specific claim(s). Relevant passages should be identified (page/column/line) where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields searched and disclosure of search scope (Rule 43.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall list the classification identification of the fields searched, and if the search extended beyond minimum documentation (to additional types of national patent literature, States, periods, or languages), the ISR shall, when practicable, identify those kinds of documents, States, periods, and languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the identification is based on a non-IPC classification, the ISA shall publish the classification used. If electronic databases were used, the ISR may indicate the database name and, where useful and practicable, the search terms used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of rectifications of obvious mistakes (Rule 43.6 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rectification of an obvious mistake authorized under Rule 91.1 shall, subject to conditions, be taken into account by the ISA for purposes of the international search and the ISR shall indicate this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rectification is authorized or notified after the ISA has begun to draw up the ISR, it need not be taken into account; the ISR should indicate this where possible, otherwise the International Bureau is to be notified and will act per Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks concerning unity of invention in ISR (Rule 43.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant paid additional fees or the search was made on the main invention only (or on less than all inventions), the ISR shall indicate what parts of the application were and were not searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISR must transparently report any restriction or limitation of the search related to unity or fee payments (Article 17(3)(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Named authorized officer on ISR (Rule 43.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall indicate the name of the officer of the ISA responsible for that report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accountability and point of contact by naming the responsible ISA officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional matter or opinions in ISR (Rule 43.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall contain no matter other than that specified in the listed Rules and shall not contain any expressions of opinion, reasoning, arguments, or explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative Instructions may permit inclusion of additional specified matter, but the ISR must avoid substantive commentary beyond prescribed items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form requirements of ISR (Rule 43.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical requirements as to the form of the ISR shall be prescribed by the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Administrative Instructions for layout, formatting, and physical presentation of the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion of the ISA (Rule 43 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the same time as establishing the ISR or the declaration under Article 17(2)(a), the ISA shall establish a written opinion as to whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step (non-obvious), and to be industrially applicable, and whether the application complies with the Treaty and Regulations insofar as checked by the ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written opinion may include other observations as provided in the Regulations and is subject to application of specified Articles and Rules mutatis mutandis. The written opinion notifies the applicant that it will be considered a written opinion of the IPEA if a demand is filed, inviting a written reply before the Rule 54 bis.1(a) time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of ISR/declaration and written opinion (Rule 44.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA shall, on the same day it establishes the ISR or declaration and the written opinion, transmit one copy of each to the International Bureau and one copy to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simultaneous transmittal ensures applicants and the IB receive ISR and written opinion promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title or abstract approval in the ISR (Rule 44.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR shall either state that the ISA approves the title and abstract as submitted by the applicant or be accompanied by the text of the title and/or abstract as established by the ISA under Rules 37 and 38.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISA may formally approve or supply its own established title/abstract text for publication and records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited documents — requests and costs (Rule 44.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for copies of cited documents may be presented any time during seven years from the international filing date. The ISA may require payment of the cost of preparing and mailing copies; the level of cost is provided in agreements between ISAs and the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies may be prepared through another agency responsible to the ISA; costs and arrangements are governed by agreements under Article 16(3)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Preliminary Report on Patentability by the ISA / IB issuance (Rule 44 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless an international preliminary examination report has been or is to be established, the International Bureau shall issue a report on behalf of the ISA as to the matters referred to in Rule 43 bis.1; the report shall have the same contents as the written opinion and bear the title 'international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter I of the Patent Cooperation Treaty)' and indicate it is issued by the IB on behalf of the ISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IB shall promptly transmit one copy of the report to the applicant; translation and communication provisions apply as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and observations on translations (Rules 44 bis.2–4, 45.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where required, translations of reports/written opinions shall be prepared by or under responsibility of the IB; translations into English may be provided to designated Offices or authorities upon request, and applicants may make written observations on correctness of translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB transmits translations to interested designated Offices and the applicant, and handles translation timelines (e.g., two months from receipt of request). Applicants' observations must be sent to interested designated Offices and the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to translate ISRs/declarations into English (Rule 45.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: International search reports and declarations under Article 17(2)(a) shall, when not in English, be translated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures accessibility in English; other translation provisions in the Rules may also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary international search request timing and eligibility (Rule 45 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may, at any time prior to expiration of 22 months from the priority date, request a supplementary international search by an ISA competent under Rule 45 bis.9; requests may be made in respect of more than one such Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be submitted to the International Bureau and identify applicant/agent, title, filing date, application number, Authority requested, and whether any translation furnished to the receiving Office is to form the basis of the supplementary search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and accompanying material for supplementary search request (Rule 45 bis.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, the supplementary search request shall be accompanied by a translation into a language accepted by the Authority if neither the filing language nor a furnished translation is accepted, and preferably an electronic sequence listing if required by the Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide translations and electronic sequence listings as required to avoid the request being considered not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary search handling fee (Rule 45 bis.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplementary search request is subject to payment of a supplementary search handling fee for the benefit of the International Bureau as set out in the Schedule of Fees; fees to be paid in designated currencies and may be refunded under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handling fee must be paid to the IB within one month from receipt of the request; refunds occur if the application or request is withdrawn before transmission of specified documents to the Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary search fee payable to the Authority (Rule 45 bis.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Authority carrying out supplementary international searches may require payment of a supplementary search fee for its own benefit; the fee is collected by the International Bureau, with Rules 16.1(b)–(e) applying mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits and amounts apply; refunds may be available if search not started or request declared not submitted under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking, correction of defects, and late payment fee for supplementary search requests (Rule 45 bis.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt the IB shall check compliance with requirements and invite correction within one month. If fees are unpaid, IB shall invite payment and charge a late payment fee equal to 50% of the supplementary search handling fee; failure to correct or pay leads to declaration the request was not submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should promptly respond to IB invitations to avoid loss of submission status; late payment fee calculation and one-month correction periods are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start, basis and scope of supplementary international search (Rule 45 bis.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search shall start promptly upon receipt of required documents (or may delay until additional documents or until 22 months from priority date). The search is based on the international application as filed or an accepted translation and shall take due account of the ISR and written opinion where available; Authority may exclude claims not subject of the international search or decide not to establish a supplementary ISR if Article 17(2)(a) declaration exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary search shall cover at least the documentation indicated in the applicable agreement; Authority may restrict search to certain claims consistent with limitations/conditions; if a limitation wholly excludes search, request is considered not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention procedure for supplementary search (Rule 45 bis.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority finds lack of unity, it shall establish the supplementary ISR on the parts relating to the 'main invention', notify the applicant with reasons, inform about possibility to request review within one month, and may charge a review fee for review by persons other than the original decision-maker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If review finds opinion entirely unjustified, supplementary ISR on all parts is established and review fee refunded; partial findings lead to appropriate notifications and possible partial searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form rules applicable to supplementary ISR (Rule 45 bis.7 and 45 bis.3(d)/(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For establishing the supplementary ISR, specified rules applicable to ISRs (e.g., Rule 43.1, 43.2, 43.5, 43.6, 43.6 bis, 43.8, 43.10) apply mutatis mutandis; supplementary ISR need not repeat citations already in ISR except where necessary; supplementary ISR may contain explanations regarding citations and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 43.9 applies mutatis mutandis except references to certain rules are non-existent; applicants and Authorities must follow the mutatis mutandis application of ISR content rules to supplementary ISRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for establishment of supplementary ISR (Rule 45 bis.7(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search shall, within 28 months from the priority date, establish the supplementary international search report or make the applicable declaration that no supplementary ISR will be established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the 28-month maximum timeline for issuing the supplementary ISR unless a declaration is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal and effect of supplementary ISR (Rule 45 bis.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority shall on the same day transmit one copy of the supplementary ISR (or declaration) to the IB and one copy to the applicant; subject to conditions, Article 20(1) and certain Rules apply as if the supplementary ISR were part of the ISR, but it need not be taken into account by the IPEA if received after it began drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely transmission is required for designated Offices to consider the supplementary ISR; lateness may limit its effect in international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence of International Searching Authorities for supplementary searches (Rule 45 bis.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ISA is competent to carry out supplementary international searches if its preparedness to do so is stated in the applicable agreement under Article 16(3)(b), subject to limitations and conditions in that agreement. The ISA that carried out the international search under Article 16(1) may not carry out the supplementary search for that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations may include subject-matter restrictions, caps on number of supplementary searches in a period, and limits on number of claims covered; applicants must select Authorities competent under the agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for amendment of claims before the International Bureau (Rule 46.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit under Article 19 for amendments before the International Bureau is two months from transmittal of the ISR to the IB and applicant, or 16 months from the priority date, whichever expires later, subject to technical preparation caveat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments received after the applicable time limit may be considered received on the last day if they reach the IB before publication technical preparations are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file amendments under Article 19 (Rule 46.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under Article 19 shall be filed directly with the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file Article 19 amendments with receiving Offices or ISAs; file with the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of amendments (Rule 46.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was filed in a language other than the language of publication, any amendment under Article 19 must be in the language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments are submitted in the publication language to be accepted by the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under Article 19(1) length and content limits (Rule 46.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement under Article 19(1) shall be in the publication language and shall not exceed 500 words if in English (or translated into English); it shall be identified by a heading (e.g., 'Statement under Article 19(1)'). The statement shall contain no disparaging comments on the ISR or relevance of its citations; reference to citations may only be made in connection with an amendment of that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the statement concise, respectful, and focused on amendments rather than criticizing the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of amendments — replacement sheets and accompanying letter (Rule 46.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under Article 19 require submission of replacement sheet(s) containing a complete set of claims in replacement of all claims originally filed, accompanied by a letter identifying claims that differ, claims cancelled, and indicating the basis for amendments in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear mapping between original and amended claims and cite the support in the originally filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication to designated Offices procedure and timing (Rule 47.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication under Article 20 shall be effected by the International Bureau to each designated Office in accordance with Rule 93 bis.1 but, subject to Rule 47.4, not prior to the international publication of the international application. The IB shall also notify each designated Office of receipt of the record copy and any priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices are generally not to receive Article 20 communications prior to publication unless express request procedures apply; IB handles notifications of document receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required for communication prepared by the IB (Rule 47.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies required for communication to designated Offices shall be prepared by the International Bureau, with further details to be provided in the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and Offices should rely on the IB to prepare required copies; check Administrative Instructions for technical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of international application communicated to designated Offices (Rule 47.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application communicated under Article 20 shall be in the language in which it is published; where publication language differs from filing language, the IB shall furnish to any designated Office, upon request, a copy in the filing language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices may request the filing-language copy if needed for national processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express request under Article 23(2) prior to international publication (Rule 47.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant makes an express request to a designated Office under Article 23(2) prior to international publication, the IB shall promptly effect the communication provided for in Article 20 to that Office upon request of the applicant or designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may expedite early communications to designated Offices by making express requests under Article 23(2).
